A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SWE-RL and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Relocated material can be matched reliably, and the revisions do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original SWE-bench evaluations, out-of-domain benchmark results, scaling experiments, reward ablations, and an auxiliary 8B midtraining experiment.

after.justification: V2 retains original SWE-RL evaluations and ablations and additionally reports the SFT model's end-to-end SWE-bench result.

M1.justification: V2 removes the distinct Llama3-Midtrain-8B approach from v1 Appendix C, including dialogue-based continued pretraining, loss masking, dynamic context adjustment, and staged annealing. This removes an entire auxiliary methodological branch. The central SWE-RL reward, GRPO procedure, and Agentless Mini inference remain unchanged.

E1.justification: SWE-bench Verified and all five out-of-domain benchmark families remain unchanged. Removing the auxiliary midtraining study narrows training-task coverage by dropping direct learning from chronological PR dialogues, including PRs without linked issues. The newly disclosed 273k RL seed count does not establish changed dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes Llama3-Midtrain-8B and adds Llama3-SWE-SFT-70B to the end-to-end comparison. Although SFT already appeared in other experiments, its participation here is new. The comparator sets in Tables 2 and 3 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 removes the complete auxiliary 8B training configuration: 500B midtraining tokens with a 32k context, annealing over the final 10%, and 8B SFT tokens with a 64k context. The retained RL and evaluation protocols remain unchanged, including 1,600 training steps and the main evaluation's 500 repair samples and 30 reproduction tests. Newly stated seed counts and optimizer information are disclosures, not demonstrated setting changes.

E4.justification: The repair/test sampling analysis, continuous-versus-discrete reward ablation, training curves, and reasoning case studies retain the same evidence. The deleted midtraining experiment is a separate model study rather than an ablation merely because it appeared in an appendix.

E5.justification: V2 Section 3.5 adds an Eval Arena-based significance discussion, benchmark-specific thresholds, and a claim of aggregate significance at the 0.05 level. Its checklist also explains the absence of SWE-bench error bars. Neither version supplies repeated-training-run counts or seed-based uncertainty estimates; the new aggregation procedure is not detailed.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds the SFT model's 36.2% end-to-end result, removes the midtraining model's 31.0%, and changes SWE-Fixer-72B from 30.2% to 32.8%. These are distinct result changes, not an improvement of the same model from 31.0% to 36.2%. The RL score remains 41.0%, and Tables 2–3 and the scaling/reward results are unchanged. The midtraining capability-degradation finding is also removed.

T1.justification: The reward definition, GRPO objective, and patch-reranking formula retain their mathematical meaning. V2 explicitly writes the normalized-advantage formula already described in v1 and changes rollout notation; these are explanatory refinements. Neither version presents theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: RL on software evolution data, a 41.0% SWE-bench Verified result, and transfer to general reasoning tasks. The added end-to-end SFT result supports an existing claim rather than redefining the contributions.

C2.justification: V2 removes the explicit limitation that high inference sampling budgets may be impractical for projects with expensive execution, while retaining the semantic-reward, localization-context, and pipeline limitations. It also removes the future-work paragraph. The new significance discussion qualifies the interpretation of small individual benchmark gains while asserting aggregate evidence.

D1.justification: The extensive midtraining reproduction recipe in v1 Appendix C disappears. Conversely, v2 newly specifies 273k RL seeds, Adam, 512 NVIDIA H100 GPUs, and approximately 32 training hours. Its checklist newly states that reward/evaluation code is supplied separately while training data and the training pipeline cannot yet be shared. These substantially change the documented reproducibility information without establishing changes to retained experiments.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Adam and Eval-Arena and removes the midtraining-related references to Fewer Truncations Improve Language Modeling and MiniCPM. The related-work discussion and positioning against SFT-based software agents otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most retained prose and the main narrative remain closely matched. V2 moves raw PR curation from Section 2.1 to Appendix A, adjusts appendix organization, removes the future-work paragraph, and adds the NeurIPS checklist. Wording, affiliations, and mathematical explanations receive localized edits rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the branded opening page with a conference layout and extensively changes typography, margins, figure sizing, and table-caption placement. The curation diagram moves from main-text Figure 2 to appendix Figure 6; the two midtraining diagrams disappear. Table 1 changes row membership, while the retained experimental plots preserve their content.

improvement.justification: The added end-to-end SFT comparison, 36.2% versus RL's 41.0% in Table 1, strengthens support for the central claim beyond v1's repair-only comparison. Newly disclosed seed and compute information improves transparency. These gains are limited by the loss of the auxiliary midtraining study and explicit sampling-cost caveat, and the new aggregate significance claim remains under-specified. Overall, the retained core study is modestly better supported and documented.
